component.name: OpenConvert
component.summary: Convert any file into anything, on your machine

description.p: OpenConvert converts files on your own machine. Around 20 formats across images, audio, video, documents, archives and tabular data, with the plan shown before the conversion runs: which engine, which steps, lossless or lossy, and how long it takes.

Every third-party engine runs inside an operating-system sandbox. On Linux that is Landlock path rules, a seccomp-bpf filter that denies AF_INET and AF_INET6 at socket(2), an empty network namespace, cgroup v2 memory and CPU limits, and no_new_privs. Engines receive open file descriptors and never a filename, so a filename cannot be an injection vector. A machine that cannot deny an engine the network does not convert; there is no configuration key that lowers that.

Nothing you already have is overwritten. Every file is created with O_EXCL, no truncating open exists anywhere in the codebase, and a source scan fails the build if one appears. An archive member named after a file you already have lands beside it with a suffix.

Every output carries a receipt: the engine and its version, the operation class, the limits applied, the confinement the worker read back about itself, the metadata removed, and the hash of the bytes actually read.

There is no telemetry, no account and no upload. One network call exists: a weekly signed manifest carrying the engine revocation list, sending no identifier, no version and no query. It is previewable in settings and can be switched off.

On-device AI for text recognition, transcription and background removal is an optional separate download of about 500 MB. Conversion works in full without it, and every model is permissively licensed and hash-pinned.

ul.li: Images: PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, HEIC, AVIF, JPEG XL and SVG.
Camera RAW decode for CR3, NEF, ARW and DNG.
Audio: WAV, FLAC, MP3 and Ogg, with FLAC and WAV round-tripping bit-identically at their own sample width.
Video containers: MKV, WebM and MP4, copying streams byte-for-byte when the codecs carry.
Documents: PDF page rendering. Archives: ZIP and TAR.
Tabular: CSV and JSON, with values kept as literal text.
Landlock and seccomp-bpf confinement, verified engaged by the workers themselves rather than claimed by the host.
A receipt beside every output, and a batch journal that resumes an interrupted run.
